entities.title: Check that the name rules stay identical to the other games'
entities.summary: src/name.ts has the same rules as Samosa's, Hivestorm's and Rally's copies, and nothing checks that they stay the same.
entities.compromise: The rules are copied into each game rather than shared; Shatterbelt's copy carries no comment asking to keep it identical, only the README's statement that the rules are Samosa's and Hivestorm's.
entities.cost: A name valid on one game's table could be refused or shown differently by another's.
acceptanceCriteria: A check fails when cleanName's rules differ between the games, or the rules are shared from one place.

origin.description: The high-score section: names are cleaned by src/name.ts, the same rules as Samosa and Hivestorm.

relationships.description: If the owner chooses to share the code (games/.dev/decisions.json, shared-game-kit).

entities.title: Give Shatterbelt a src/ui folder like Rally's and Hivestorm's
entities.summary: render.ts, input.ts and sound.ts sit beside main.ts in src/, where the other web games keep them in src/ui/, and the Scene machine is run by main.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: render.ts, input.ts and sound.ts are in src/ui/, with that folder's component and class diagrams; render.ts is split where it holds separate concerns.
The Scene machine is in src/ui/ with its state diagram, named Screen like Rally's; main.ts only wires things together.
npm test passes, and play is unchanged.

origin.description: The owner asked for a plan to refactor retro-games so that it shows everything the cyberspace explorer can show, and approved its Phase 0.
